paper.central_claim: MetaAgent: starting from a minimal reason-plus-help-seeking workflow with a tool router, an agent that after each task distills self-reflection and ground-truth-verified reflection into a concise experience text carried into later contexts, and builds an in-house persistent knowledge base from its tool-use history ('meta tool learning', no parameter updates), outperforms workflow-based baselines and matches or exceeds end-to-end trained agents on GAIA, WebWalkerQA and BrowseComp.
paper.title: MetaAgent: Toward Self-Evolving Agent via Tool Meta-Learning

reason: Full text read; non-weight, retained experience text and persistent knowledge base are updated from task outcomes and read in later tasks: in scope as system_method. E.causality left unknown because ablation values (Figure 3) are not observable in the pinned material; controller may supply the Figure 3 page image.

evidence.quote: As MetaAgent solves tasks, it continually conducts self-reflection and answer verification, distilling actionable experience into concise texts that are dynamically incorporated into future task contexts.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained object: a concise experience text conditioning later contexts.

evidence.quote: Second, if ground-truth answers are available, verified reflection compares the predicted answer
evidence.support_explanation: Verified reflection uses the gold answer of the task just solved.

evidence.quote: Verified reflection is only performed after the answer is finalized, and the updated experience is used exclusively in subsequent tasks to prevent information leakage.
evidence.support_explanation: Same-item leakage guard only; gold labels of earlier benchmark items feed later items.

evidence.quote: In our experiments, experience is constructed online from scratch, ensuring no information leakage during evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Learning stream is the evaluation stream (online on the benchmark).

evidence.quote: we initialize the in-house tool by simulating task completion three times for each benchmark, thereby proactively gathering and constructing the persistent memory required by MetaAgent
evidence.support_explanation: Knowledge base is pre-populated by running the benchmark's own questions three times before scored runs: extra search budget and test-question exposure not given to baselines.

evidence.quote: If MetaAgent lacks confidence in its reasoning process or the concluded answer, the self-reflection experience
evidence.support_explanation: Low-confidence self-reflection triggers a within-task retry (extra attempt).
Best trained baseline: GAIA 48.5 exceeds MetaAgent 47.6.

evidence.quote: we use 103 questions from the text-only validation subset
evidence.support_explanation: GAIA evaluation set is 103 questions, so one question is about 1 point (Level 3 has 12 questions).

evidence.quote: we evaluate on two selected topics, Art and History , totaling 257 questions
evidence.support_explanation: BrowseComp is a 257-question cost-driven subset; 7.1 vs 2.7 is about 18 vs 7 questions.

evidence.quote: (1) removing self reflection (w/o self reflection); (2) removing verified reflection (w/o verified reflection); (3) removing the use of in-house tools (w/o in-house tool); (4) using only the minimal workflow
evidence.support_explanation: Store/loop-off ablations exist but only as Figure 3 on GAIA; bar values are not in the text.

evidence.quote: both self-reflection and verified reflection are critical, and their combination forms a meta tool learning loop that substantially boosts performance
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative claim with no numbers in text.

evidence.quote: Ablation Study. Key components of MetaAgent are individually removed and evaluated on the GAIA benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Ablations restricted to the 103-question GAIA set.

evidence.quote: For all baselines, we either report the results from original papers or run the official implementations.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline provenance is mixed and per-baseline source is not stated.

evidence.quote: Informed by this self-reflection, MetaAgent launches a second attempt
evidence.support_explanation: Within-task retry gives MetaAgent extra search attempts versus single-pass baselines.
Backbone swap on GAIA only; not a causal control for evolution.

evidence.quote: MetaAgent incrementally constructs an in-house tool—a persistent local knowledge base
evidence.support_explanation: Second retained object: raw tool-interaction content cache (BGE-m3 index).
From GAIA split sizes (about 39/52/12 questions) the reported percentages give 49 solved for MetaAgent and 50 for WebThinker-RL: the GAIA average gap is one question.
Related work covers RAG, agentic search, workflow and RL-trained agents; no memory/experience-reflection agents (e.g. reflection-memory or insight-store agents) are discussed or compared.

signatures.object: Single cumulative natural-language experience text E carried in the agent input X_t = {q, p, E_{t-1}}
signatures.information: Trajectory and final answer; gold answer (verified reflection) when available; previous E; self-reflection without labels when confidence low
signatures.operation: LLM reflection function Omega rewrites E from (X, Y, A*, E_{t-1}); self-reflection summary added to input for a retry
signatures.output: Updated E (concise strategies for planning and tool use)
signatures.conditions: Gold answers available for the stream; E prepended wholesale to later tasks
signatures.feedback: Ground-truth comparison (verified) and model's own confidence (self)
signatures.selection_rule/data: None reported: every Omega rewrite is accepted; no validation of the new E against a held-out set
signatures.persistence: E persists across tasks in the stream
signatures.later_use: Prepended to the next task's input
signatures.failure_boundary: No maintenance (size, conflict, forgetting, rollback); gold-label dependence; same stream for learning and scoring

signatures.object: In-house tool: persistent vector index (BGE-m3) of all content the tool router touched
signatures.information: Raw web pages and tool outputs from all tool calls
signatures.operation: Append all external knowledge to C; initialize C by simulating each benchmark's tasks three times; agent can query C later
signatures.conditions: Pre-pass over the benchmark's own questions
signatures.feedback: None (no outcome signal, no utility measure)
signatures.claimed_effect: Mitigates single-pass search information loss, especially on BrowseComp
signatures.failure_boundary: Pre-pass exposes the test questions' evidence; not outcome-grounded experience

gap.author_gap: Workflow-based agents rely on hand-designed strategies and cannot adapt; end-to-end trained agents need costly annotated data and may degrade elsewhere. Proposed: a minimal workflow that evolves through experience.
gap.checked_gap: The fixed object (expert-written strategies in prompts/workflows) is named and is a legitimate target, but related work never addresses agents that already learn text experience or memory from outcomes, so the residual versus those neighbors is not established.
gap.lineage/closest_adjacent: Cited neighbors: Search-o1, WebThinker, Search-R1, DeepResearcher, Mind-Map agent. Missing from the pinned text: reflection-memory / insight-store agents, which are the direct ancestors of the experience mechanism.
gap.residue: Not stated relative to experience-learning agents.
gap.method_response: Reflection-distilled experience text plus persistent tool-use knowledge base on a minimal router-based workflow.
gap.remaining_gap: No maintenance or gating of E or C; gold labels required; evaluation on the learning stream.
unresolved: Whether experience-text accumulation is new relative to reflection/insight-store agents cannot be assessed from the pinned material

G.reason: Fixed object (hand-written strategies/workflows) is named but the nearest neighbors for the actual mechanism (agents that distill outcome reflections into text memory) are absent from related work, so no residual bottleneck against them is established; problem statement is generic.

M.reason: Concrete loop (reflect with gold answer, rewrite E, prepend; cache tool content) with an intuitive causal story, but the rewrite function, retention policy and the reason monolithic rewrite avoids collapse are unspecified; reliance on gold answers and pre-pass undermines the learning story.

X.reason: Write path (Eq.7) and read path (prepend E, query C) are described, but Omega prompt, E size control, update schedule, task order, retry limits and any gate/versioning/rollback are missing; information permissions (gold answers during the stream) are partly explicit.

E.measurement.reason: EM on GAIA/BrowseComp and LLM-equivalence on WebWalkerQA follow official settings, but test sets are small or cost-driven subsets, the equivalence judge is not specified, and baseline numbers have mixed provenance.

E.causality.reason: The only controls that could isolate the retained experience and knowledge base are the Figure 3 ablations, whose values are not in the pinned text; Table 1 and Table 2 comparisons do not isolate evolution and are confounded by pre-pass and retries. Rating withheld pending the Figure 3 page image.

E.holdout.reason: Only same-item leakage is prevented; experience is learned online from gold answers of earlier benchmark questions and the knowledge base is built by solving the benchmark questions three times, so learning stream equals evaluation stream with no held-out split.

E.statistics.reason: Set sizes are stated and mixed results are reported, but single runs without intervals; GAIA margin to the best trained baseline is one question of 103 and Level 3 has 12 questions.

E.cost.reason: No tokens, tool calls, wall time or reflection cost are reported even though the system adds three pre-passes, retries and per-task reflection; only the hardware (eight A100) is mentioned.
